_about: Real searches, held to the real bills they must and must not return. preflight reads this twice:
under --code the bills below are the fixture, with search_index.json (what their own analyses and
texts are about), run through the matcher build_pages cuts out of app.js; with site/idx and
site/sidx built, the same cases run over the real index of the term, where at_most catches a flood,
every term of the table is looked for in every term's titles and texts, and a retitled bill is reported.
Nothing here is typed. python3 build_search_index.py --fixture tests/search_cases.json copies every
bill's title, sponsor, committees and topic from site/idx, cuts search_index.json out of the term's
real search index for exactly these bills, and copies the text of the few bills listed under "texts"
into search_texts.json. Add a bill by naming its id in a case and running that: an invented title
proves nothing.
must = the search has to list it. first = it has the reader's own word, so it is listed above every
must bill, which the table found. never = plainly about something else. at_most = a ceiling on the
real index. same = each group is two sides' words for one subject and must return one list.
nothing = a real word no bill of the term is about: it must list nothing and be offered as no
other word. offer = a misspelling: it must list nothing as typed, the page must offer that word,
and must and never are then held to the offered word's list. near = bills that tempt a wrong
reading (titles that say 'invest', for 'incest'), named so that the fixture carries them.
known = real words that were once read as other words; each must be in sidx/words.json.
top = it must be among the first five listed (over the real index). across = searches run
over every term's bills (the real index only), each bill named with the year it was filed.
Machine-judged, by reading titles and, where a title did not settle it, the bill's text. It is a
seed, not the person's reference: the person's own judgments belong in the bench.
